title: Social distance in images

draft.title: Social distance in images
card: Social distance is how close a subject seems to the viewer. The creator picks it by choosing how much of the subject fills the frame.
shows a face or one small thing. It feels personal, as if we are near the subject and can see their feelings.
shows a person from about the waist up. It feels social, like meeting someone in a friendly but not private way.
shows the whole subject with lots of space around it. It keeps the viewer at a distance, like a stranger watching from far away.
draft.remember: The closer the shot, the closer we feel to the subject. The further away, the more distant we feel.

a.q: A film shows a girl's tearful face filling the whole screen. What does this close-up mostly make the viewer feel?
opts: Close to her and aware of her feelings
Like a stranger watching her from far away
That she is one person among many in a crowd
That she is more powerful than the viewer
a.why: A close-up fills the frame with the face, so the viewer feels near the girl and can see her feelings. A long shot, not a close-up, would keep the viewer far away.
a.clue: Think about how near the face seems.

b.q: A poster for a camping trip shows a tiny tent far away in a huge, empty valley. Which shot is this, and what is its effect?
opts: A long shot, which keeps the viewer at a distance
A close-up, which makes the scene feel personal
A mid shot, which makes the scene feel social
A long shot, which makes the viewer feel very close
b.why: The whole tent is shown with lots of space around it, so this is a long shot. A long shot keeps the viewer at a distance, so feeling very close is the opposite of its effect.
b.clue: Look at how much space surrounds the tent.

a.best: Close to her and aware of her feelings

b.best: A long shot, which keeps the viewer at a distance
